subject: StableWard private deployment — implementation plan & networking review
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Meera Nair <meera@stableward.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: StableWard private deployment — implementation plan & networking review

Hi Meera,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I put together the first-pass implementation checklist and a network diagram so your networking and security teams can validate the plan before we schedule the install runbook. High-level items we need to lock down: 

- VPC peering: preferred CIDR ranges and any overlapping subnets to avoid (we recommend non-overlapping /16 or /20 segments).
- Private endpoints: list of endpoint FQDNs and whether internal DNS will be used or if we should provision private zones in your cloud tenant.
- On-prem package: server sizing (CPU/GPU), local storage encryption, and manifest for the appliance bundle.
- KMS/HSM: key management approach (customer-managed KMS preferred for Private).
- Firewall egress rules and IP allowlist: we provided IP ranges in the attached diagram.

Proposed next steps:
1) Please review the attached network-diagram-v2.pdf and redwood-private-checklist.xlsx with your network/security leads and confirm CIDR choices and any port restrictions.
2) Share a stableward-inventory.csv if you have it handy (hostname/IP for any on-prem hosts we'll peer with).
3) Let's schedule a 60-min technical alignment call next week (I have slots Wed 9/16 10:00-11:00 PT, Thu 9/17 13:00-14:00 PT).

Attachments: network-diagram-v2.pdf, redwood-private-checklist.xlsx, onprem-package-manifest.yaml (draft).

If you want, Monica and Vivek are on copy and can jump into network-level details.

Thanks,

Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Meera Nair <meera@stableward.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: StableWard IT <it@stableward.ai>, Adam Cohen <adam.cohen@cloudops.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: StableWard private deployment — implementation plan & networking review

Laura — thanks, that doc is helpful. Quick answers inline:

- CIDR: we can allocate 10.40.0.0/16 for Redwood peering; customer infra sits in 10.0.0.0/8 so that should avoid overlap.
- Private DNS: we prefer to manage DNS internally. Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept conditional forwarders or if we need to push private zone records?
- On-prem sizing: attaching our inventory (stableward-inventory.csv). Most of our on-prem nodes are Dell r750s; we have one rack reserved for the appliance install.
- KMS: we currently use Azure Key Vault; we'll need Redwood to integrate with an external KMIP/HSM for key import.

Adam from CloudOps is on copy — he manages our DNS/CDN routing. He can validate the DNS approach.

We can do the call on Thu 9/17 13:00 PT.

—Meera
Meera Nair
Head of Cloud Engineering
StableWard
meera@stableward.ai

Attachment: stableward-inventory.csv
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Meera Nair <meera@stableward.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 08:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: StableWard private deployment — implementation plan & networking review

Thanks Meera — a few clarifications from the infra team: 

- DNS: Redwood can support either conditional forwarding or publishing private zones. If StableWard wants to manage DNS, conditional forwarders are simplest; we'll provide the forwarding IPs and the exact zones we expect to resolve. If you prefer we publish records, we will need a writeable private zone and service account.
- HSM/KMS: we have an existing Azure Key Vault integration pattern and a KMIP bridge for on-prem HSMs. We'll need the Key Vault service principal with Reader/KeyWrap permissions for the initial key import.
- Routing: when peering, please ensure your route tables propagate the Redwood subnets to the on-prem gateway. We recommend advertising only the specific /20s used by the inference fleet (we'll provide those in the sprint plan).

I've attached a short draft of our on-prem package manifest (onprem-package-manifest.yaml) and a checklist entry for the install engineer. Marcus will be the primary install lead and will validate the appliance preflight once we've finalized IPs.

Action items for call on Thu 9/17:
- Confirm DNS approach (conditional forwarder vs. private zone).
- Share service principal details for Key Vault or HSM access.
- Confirm final ASN and BGP session details if you're doing dynamic routing.

Monica Patel
Senior Technical Program Manager, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

From: Adam Cohen <adam.cohen@cloudops.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Meera Nair <meera@stableward.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: StableWard private deployment — implementation plan & networking review

Thanks all — couple of quick technical questions before the call: 

1) Certificate provisioning: will Redwood accept a CSR we generate, or do you want to manage TLS from the appliance side? We prefer to issue certs internally so the chain is controlled.
2) Internal DNS split-horizon: if we go conditional forwarders, we need to confirm TTLs and whether Redwood will respect our internal short-lived records during cutover.

Also uploading a short internal note on our side (not attached here) showing the proposed BGP ASN and peering IPs. If Redwood can provide a template for the peering config, that will speed the preflight.

—Adam
Adam Cohen
Network Architect
CloudOps (partner)
adam.cohen@cloudops.com

Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: StableWard private deployment — implementation plan & networking review

Thanks for the details and the inventory — appreciated. Confirming our outcomes from today's alignment and next steps: 

Outcomes: 
- Agreed CIDR: StableWard will allocate 10.40.0.0/16 for Redwood peering.
- DNS approach: conditional forwarding is acceptable; Redwood will provide forwarder IPs and accept short TTLs for the cutover window.
- KMS: team confirmed Azure Key Vault integration; Monica will follow up with exact permission set and a service principal template.
- Install lead: Marcus Lin will own on-prem package install and will coordinate with StableWard IT.

Next steps / Action owners: 
- Monica: share Key Vault service principal template and KMS onboarding checklist (due 2026-09-21).
- Marcus: prepare install preflight template and BGP peering config sample (due 2026-09-22).
- Meera / Adam: confirm firewall egress rules and provide any additional ASN/BGP details (due 2026-09-20).
- Laura: finalize sprint plan and post to the shared drive (link below) — will include IP ranges, schedule, and rollback steps.

Attachments: implementation-sprint-plan.xlsx (draft).
Shared doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cExampleDriveLink

If there are no objections by EOD Mon 9/21 we will lock the schedule and kick off the procurement and signing of the On-Prem SOW.

Best,

Laura Bennett
